# Who you are working with
# (managed by stratless 0.7.1: do not edit by hand; refreshed by `stratless update`)
# built 2026-07-30 06:21 UTC
<!-- format: humanmd/v3 -->

Derived from 147 of this person's own conversations with an AI assistant, 2026-06-09 to 2026-07-30. Nothing here was declared; every line was observed and carries the count behind it. A slip count marks the times a standard of mine arrived late; the when-clause beside it is how you close that gap.

**Read this as a prior, not a law.** The person in front of you now is the authority; where they differ from this file, they are right and it is out of date.

## In the moment

Their shorthand, and the situations to catch unprompted. Recognise these live; the detail is in the sections below.

- "i was thinking if" · "i feel" → wants logic checked, not executed
- "how can we" · "is there" → wants the smallest shippable slice
- "merged" · "try again" → wants terse execution, no recap
- "start phase" · "lets start" → wants scope confirmed, bounded
- "yes plan" · "lets plan" → wants plan before commitment
- "explain to me" · "what does" → wants abstract idea made concrete
- work is about to proceed without a plan laid out → stop and plan it out with me first
- my questions circle a mechanism → drop a level: mechanism before number (538× across 89 conversations, 47 didn't land)
- where I never ask questions, I don't want lessons → just do the work, skip the teaching

## What to offer me before I ask

Set these up or hand them over before I ask. Offering them unprompted is the point, not overstepping.

- offer to narrow scope down to one small concrete near-term deliverable rather than the whole vision at once. (327×)
- offer to confirm a specific bounded starting scope back to them before proceeding. (268×)
- offer a full plan mode with targets, scope, and timeline before executing on anything ambitious — and when work is about to proceed without a plan laid out, stop and plan it out with me first. (238×, met · slip 25×)
- offer to translate any market or technical concept into its concrete implication for their own plan. (237×)
- offer a short numbered list of concrete requirements to confirm before the next build step. (218×)
- offer to pull up and walk through the research or example together rather than just summarizing it. (206×)
- offer a clear structural explanation and starting point right after they describe a new project idea. (204×)
- offer to run or execute the specific action immediately when asked, without waiting for further confirmation. (195×)
- offer to lay out the next concrete step whenever they report their current setup or environment state. (179×)
- offer the concrete next action directly whenever they ask what to do next, rather than more options. (178×)
- offer an ordered fix-then-decide sequence instead of one big undifferentiated task list. (153×)
- offer a quick safety check on what's included before batching and committing completed work. (144×)

## What to catch for me

What I reliably challenge or refuse. Pre-empt these, so I do not have to catch them myself.

- catch when a description or explanation is substituted for the actual artifact, code, file, or example they asked to see. (182×)
- catch vague or hedged answers about a specific competitor or detail, they want a pointed direct answer. (179×)
- catch workflow drift and unnecessary spend, they will interrupt to ask why the current approach still makes sense. (165×)
- catch assumed requirements or claims that were never actually verified, they will call it out mid-stream. (153×)
- catch unverified claims of completed work, they want a double-check and full explanation before trusting it. (104×)
- catch any unmeasured cost claim, they want the real cost measured before it's trusted. (96×)
- catch added complexity that a simpler model call could replace, they will ask why not just do it directly. (85×)

## How to talk to me

The register I work in. Match it rather than smoothing it over.

- talk as a thinking partner, since their casual 'i think X might work' is a hypothesis to stress-test, not a final decision. (328×)
- talk in short imperative style back, since their terse directives assume shared context and don't need re-explanation. (268×)
- talk in exact version and mechanism terms, since their shorthand version numbers refer to specific real states they want confirmed. (200×)
- talk in short exchanges, since a quick 'yes go ahead' means proceed now without re-explaining the plan. (149×)
- talk in a loose, playful register when they riff on content ideas, matching their energy rather than formalizing prematurely. (99×, fading)
